newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-SMALL KNOWS WHAT'S WRONG WITH SPRINGBOKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMALL KNOWS WHAT'S WRONG WITH SPRINGBOKS.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Aug 8 - The Springbok rugby team is reaping the bitter fruits of constant changes, according to winger James Small.
The South Africans' recent results, Small believed, reflected the inconsistencies of their regime since the country's international re-admission in 1992.
In their last five tests the Springboks won just one, against the British Lions who had the three-test series wrapped up 2-0 by then.
Their World Cup crown became even more uncomfortable on their head after they lost the first round Tri-Series matches to the All Blacks and the Wallabies.
Their series chances had disappeared before they arrived in New Zealand for Saturday's second round clash with the All Blacks at Eden Park.

Careful with his words and avoiding pointing a finger at anyone in case it resulted in another rebuke for him, as in 1996, the most-capped Springbok said it was sad that the team had not been allowed to grow.
"I've been around now for six years and there have been five different systems. It's hard, difficult for any team," the 28-year-old said.
"You get your team together and you kind of find your place in it, find your little comfort zone as far as living under pressure, on tours and things like that go.
"It's just something we've been learning because of certain circumstances. I'm not saying it's anybody's fault that we haven't been left together as a team.
"Look at the All Blacks, the bases are still the same for a long, long time.
"At this level you have to be consistent, you can only get that if you have a consistent selection.
"Given the fact of our environment -- new coach, new team almost -- it's a learning curve again. It's not an excuse, we're finding our feet again.
"It's always easier to get to a point rather than stay at that point. That's the lesson this team is learning."
Their Ellis Park test against the All Blacks three weeks ago was a prime example of the inconsistency he was talking about, Small, capped 41 times, said.

"Our levels dropped, our intensity dropped, the commitment levels dropped. That comes from a number of different things -- the planning, the youth or inexperience. We have to get guys to understand to try and maintain that level.
"That 23-7 lead (to the Springboks) at Ellis Park ... any experienced side would have nailed that test."
Despite their 35-32 loss, the Springboks' dressing room resembled the victors'
"We came out of Ellis Park, we knew we had given our best, the result was not in our favour but there was still a feeling of satisfaction," Small said.
"But then you're playing against the All Blacks. They're masters of playing the game for 80 minutes.
"The All Blacks came to South Africa to bowl us. People talked about the Dream Team.

"You just have a good look at the squad that came, they're just an immense looking team. They're probably the best outfit that the All Blacks have had together, and I don't want to stand on anybody's toes, ever since I've been playing or watching rugby.
"People said they would give us 30 points.
"I don't think the Springboks would ever be happy with a loss.
"But we got true satisfaction out of that game because we showed that nobody's invincible, no team is unbeatable.
"I think those are the strengths we'll draw on, on Saturday."
Small played his record-breaking 40th test as a replacement that day.
"It happened in a funny way, I came off the bench. It wasn't the greatest way it could happen."
Sadly, the South Africans forgot to acknowledge his milestone.
All Black captain Sean Fitzpatrick however mentioned it in the post-test function.

"Sean's such a class act. I really admire him. The All Black situation is one really to look up to and be respected. They have an understanding about the essence of the whole thing, which we have battled with over the years because of the changes. There's always a new system."
Of his own game, Small felt he needed to take the initiative at times to return to his old form.
"I'm happy with my work rate, I'm happy with my finishing. I think I have to get a bit selfish with the ball in my hand and actually give it horns -- back myself a bit more."
